messages:
cheng: quick heads-up — after flipping kernel_autotune.v2 in prod for continuous batching, we see a regression on long-seq workloads (>=1024). p99 token latency up ~12% on the canary pool. profile dump below, tl;dr looks like bad kernel picks + launch overhead + KV churn

sam: ugh. do we have a minimal repro or perf trace? which region/capacity? :eyes:

cheng: canary pool in us-west-2, dedicated-g4dn-like machines. here's a trimmed profiler snippet from a single request (seq=1536):
```
request_id=...
chosen_kernel=matmul_sm80_fused_fast   # v2 autotune pick
launch_ms=1.28
compute_ms=3.02
kv_cache_hits=42
kv_cache_evictions=412   # spikes during rollout window
amortized_launch_per_token_ms=0.00083
fall_back_kernel=matmul_generic
fallback_launch_ms=0.12
fallback_compute_ms=3.75
```
Note: before the change we usually hit matmul_generic with lower launch cost and slightly higher compute but overall lower p99 because continuous batching amortizes the launch.

maria: interesting — so autotuner prefers the "fast" fused kernel (better FLOP efficiency) but its launch overhead is high so for continuous batching (many small launches across seq) it's worse. we saw something similar on older Ampere configs.

aj: can you paste the scheduler metrics? are we seeing many short-lived launches (i.e., many kernels per request) or one big launch?

cheng: scheduler shows many micro-launches because of KV cache misses splitting the request into multiple segments. batching keeps aggregating but the kernel gets reselected per segment. metrics: launches_per_request 3.1 -> 4.4 during repro window.

maria: two orthogonal problems: (1) kernel selector is sequence-length aware but not amortized-launch aware; (2) segmenting + KV eviction creates extra launches which amplifies the cost. autotune needs a penalty for launch_ms when comparing kernels.

sam: can we do a quick config toggle to force the selector to prefer low-launch kernels for continuous batching? even just a heuristic: if avg_seq >= 512 and sched.continuous=true prefer low_launch_cost=true.

cheng: I pushed a feature-flag: kernel_autotune.v2.prefer_low_launch_for_continuous=true to the canary pool ~6m ago. monitoring now.

perf-bot: canary synthetic run (seq=1536, 1000q): baseline p99=145ms, before-toggle p99=160ms (+10.3%), after-toggle p99=146ms (+0.7%). CI traces attached to the job.

aj: nice. action items: 1) Maria to propose a formal autotune scoring function that includes launch_ms amortization and a hysteresis term; 2) Cheng to run a bisect to find the exact commit/param that pushed the poor picks; 3) I'll investigate KV eviction coupling and whether we can coalesce segments so kernel selection happens once per big segment.

maria: for the scoring function draft: score = alpha * compute_ms + beta * (launch_ms / expected_tokens_processed) + gamma * memory_safety_penalty. alpha/beta/gamma are per-arch trainable params. add hysteresis by requiring delta_score > hysteresis_threshold before switching kernels. also add sticky_kernel window (n seconds) for continuous sessions.

sam: +1 — are there perf counters we should expose to the tuner? launch_ms histogram, avg_tokens_processed_in_launch, kv_eviction_rate, and scheduler_coalescing_ratio would be helpful.

cheng: I'll add those to the autotune metrics endpoint. Aj, can you start a bisect job today? the window is 1827360000..1827604321 (rough range of deploys).

aj: starting bisect now. plan: run microbench + e2e with kv-heavy traces. will post a summary.

perf-bot: bisect job queued (id=bisect-182760). estimated 2h. will notify on result.

maria: once we have the offending change, we can either tweak scoring or revert the specific heuristic. long-term: train alpha/beta per-arch with augmentation for continuous batching patterns.

cheng: fyi — for immediate mitigation I recommend keeping the feature-flag on for canary and flipping it off in broader pools until we land scoring improvements. I'll open a PR with the extra metrics and the sticky_kernel window change.

sam: sounds good. please tag me on the PR and add a short ops runbook for toggling kernel_autotune flags per-region.

cheng: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
